name: Abū al-Fayḍ Muḥammad Murtaḍā al-Ḥusaynī al-Zabīdī
summary: Indian-born lexicographer of Cairo whose Tāj al-ʿarūs, the commentary on al-Fīrūzābādī's al-Qāmūs, is the largest dictionary of classical Arabic.
bio: Murtaḍā al-Zabīdī was born in Bilgram in northern India in 1145/1732, studied there and then in Zabīd in Yemen, which gave him his name, and in the Ḥijāz, and settled in Cairo in 1167/1754. He became one of the most sought-after scholars of the city, a teacher of hadith and a correspondent of scholars from the Maghrib to India.

His Tāj al-ʿarūs min jawāhir al-Qāmūs comments on al-Fīrūzābādī's dictionary word by word, adding the evidence of the older dictionaries; it is the fullest dictionary of the classical language. He died of plague in Cairo in 1205/1791.

sources.title: Zebîdî, Muhammed Murtazâ, TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
